name: discover_services
title: Discover Services
description: Discover which DreamFactory services and operations YOU (the calling agent) are permitted to access, based on your assigned role. Returns the role-filtered service catalog with the operations (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) allowed on each. Call this first to learn your boundaries before querying any data.

name: request_access
title: Request Access
description: Request access you do not currently have. Creates a pending request for human approval and notifies administrators via alerts. Provide the service names and operations you need plus an optional reason. You will NOT get access immediately — an administrator must approve it, after which a fresh scoped key is issued.

operations.description: Operations needed: any of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.

note.description: Why you need this access (shown to the approving admin).

name: list_apis
title: List Available APIs
description: List the database and file services in this connection with their category and tool-name prefix. Lighter than discover_services, which also reports the HTTP verbs your role permits on each service; call that when you need to know what you may write.

name: all_get_tables
title: Get Tables from All Databases
description: Table names from every connected database in one call, keyed by service name. Use it when you do not know which database holds the data; for one database call get_tables, and for columns and relationships call get_data_model.

name: all_find_table
title: Find Table Across All Databases
description: Look up one table name in every connected database and return its full schema from each database that has it. Use it when a table could live in several services. Returns foundIn (the services that have it) plus per-service schema or error.

table_name.description: Exact table name to look for.

name: all_get_stored_procedures
title: Get Stored Procedures from All Databases
description: Stored procedure names and parameters from every connected database, keyed by service; empty for services without procedures. For a single database call get_stored_procedures.

name: all_get_stored_functions
title: Get Stored Functions from All Databases
description: Stored function names and parameters from every connected database, keyed by service; empty for services without functions. For a single database call get_stored_functions.

name: all_get_resources
title: Get Resources from All Databases
description: Resource groups (_table, _schema, _proc, _func) exposed by every connected database, keyed by service. Use it only to compare what each service offers; all_get_tables is the lighter call when you just need tables.

name: ordersdb_get_api_spec
title: ordersdb: Get API Spec
description: [ordersdb] OpenAPI 3.0 spec for this database: endpoint paths, query-parameter syntax and, with tables=true, every table. Use it when you need exact filter/order syntax or endpoint details; get_data_model is the cheaper call for planning queries. compact=true (default) returns the token-efficient form.

resource_name.description: Get spec for a specific table/resource only

tables.description: Include full table and field details

name: ordersdb_get_data_model
title: ordersdb: Get Data Model
description: [ordersdb] BEST FIRST CALL. Condensed model of every table in one response: columns (name/type/FK), row counts, self-referencing hierarchies and junction tables. Use it to plan queries before get_table_data; reach for the per-table schema tools only when one table needs more detail.

refresh.description: Bypass the cached model and rebuild it from the database (slow on large schemas).

name: ordersdb_get_tables
title: ordersdb: List Tables
description: [ordersdb] Table names only, the cheapest schema call. Use it to confirm a table exists; get_data_model also returns columns and relationships for every table.

name: ordersdb_get_table_schema
title: ordersdb: Get Table Schema
description: [ordersdb] Full definition of ONE table: columns with types, nullability and defaults, primary and foreign keys, and the related-table aliases usable in get_table_data related=. Use it after get_data_model when one table needs closer inspection. get_table_fields returns only the column list and get_table_relationships only the relationship graph.

table_name.description: Exact table name as returned by get_tables or get_data_model.

name: ordersdb_get_table_data
title: ordersdb: Get Table Data
description: [ordersdb] Read rows from one table with filter/order/limit/offset; returns a resource array (plus meta.count when include_count is set). Max 1000 rows per call; paginate with offset for more. count_only=true returns just the count. For SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX/GROUP BY use aggregate_data — this tool cannot aggregate.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

fields.description: Columns to return (default: all). Fewer columns means a smaller response.

filter.description: SQL-like WHERE clause: field=value, field>10, field LIKE %text%, field IN (1,2), field IS NULL; combine with AND/OR in parentheses, e.g. (status=open) AND (amount>100). Use bare field names, no quotes or brackets around them.

offset.description: Rows to skip before the first returned row; combine with limit to page.

limit.description: Max records per request (server max: 1000). Use with offset to paginate.

order.description: Sort clause: "field ASC" or "field DESC", comma-separated for several, e.g. "created DESC, id ASC".

continue.description: Rarely needed on reads: continue past per-row errors in a batch instead of failing the whole request.

related.description: Include related records via FK (e.g. "parent_table_by_fk_field"). Check relationships in the data model.

count_only.description: Return only the record count, no data. Use this instead of COUNT() in fields.

include_count.description: Include total record count in response metadata alongside data.

include_schema.description: Append the table schema to the response (adds size; prefer get_table_schema).

ids.description: Primary-key values to fetch directly, instead of a filter.

name: ordersdb_create_records
title: ordersdb: Create Records
description: [ordersdb] Insert one or more rows into a table. Returns the primary key of each new row (or the columns named in fields). Not idempotent: repeating the call inserts again. To change existing rows use update_records.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

records.description: Rows to insert, one object per row keyed by column name. Omit auto-increment keys.

fields.description: Columns to return for each created row (default: primary key only).

related.description: Related-table alias whose nested records inside each row should be created too, e.g. "orders_by_customer_id".

continue.description: On a per-row error keep inserting the remaining rows and report each failure, instead of stopping at the first.

rollback.description: On any per-row error undo the rows this call already inserted (all or nothing).

name: ordersdb_update_records
title: ordersdb: Update Records
description: [ordersdb] Patch existing rows: only the columns present in each record change. Target rows one of three ways: records that each carry the primary key; ids plus a single record applied to every id; or filter plus a single record applied to every match. Returns the primary keys (or fields) of the rows changed.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

records.description: Column/value pairs to apply. One object per row when each carries its primary key; a single object when targeting by ids or filter.

fields.description: Columns to return for each updated row (default: primary key only).

related.description: Related-table alias whose nested records inside each row should be updated too.

ids.description: Primary-key values of the rows to patch with the single record.

filter.description: SQL-like filter (same syntax as get_table_data) selecting the rows to patch with the single record.

continue.description: On a per-row error keep updating the remaining rows and report each failure, instead of stopping at the first.

rollback.description: On any per-row error undo the rows this call already changed (all or nothing).

name: ordersdb_delete_records
title: ordersdb: Delete Records
description: [ordersdb] Permanently delete rows selected by ids or filter; there is no undo. A call with neither ids nor filter is refused unless force=true, which empties the whole table. Returns the primary keys of the deleted rows.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

ids.description: Primary-key values of the rows to delete.

filter.description: SQL-like filter (same syntax as get_table_data) selecting the rows to delete.

force.description: true deletes EVERY row in the table when no ids or filter are given. Never set it casually.

fields.description: Columns of each deleted row to return (default: primary key only).

related.description: Related-table alias whose records should be included in the response for each deleted row.

continue.description: On a per-row error keep deleting the remaining rows and report each failure, instead of stopping at the first.

rollback.description: On any per-row error restore the rows this call already deleted (all or nothing).

name: ordersdb_get_table_fields
title: ordersdb: Get Table Fields
description: [ordersdb] Column list for one table: name, type, length, nullable, default, primary/foreign-key flags. Lighter than get_table_schema, which also returns constraints and related tables; get_data_model already lists these columns for every table.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

refresh.description: Bypass the schema cache and re-read from the database.

name: ordersdb_get_table_relationships
title: ordersdb: Get Table Relationships
description: [ordersdb] Relationships of one table: foreign keys in and out, self-referencing hierarchies (parent_id-style trees) and junction tables for many-to-many. Use it to pick the related= alias for get_table_data; get_data_model summarizes the same relationships for every table.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

refresh.description: Bypass the schema cache and re-read from the database.

name: ordersdb_get_stored_procedures
title: ordersdb: List Stored Procedures
description: [ordersdb] List the stored procedures this database exposes, with their parameter names and types, callable through call_stored_procedure. Empty on databases without procedures (e.g. SQLite).

name: ordersdb_call_stored_procedure
title: ordersdb: Call Stored Procedure
description: [ordersdb] Execute a stored procedure by name with named parameters and return its result sets and output parameters. Procedures can modify data: check what the procedure does (get_stored_procedures) before calling it.

procedure_name.description: Procedure name exactly as listed by get_stored_procedures.

parameters.description: Input parameters keyed by parameter name.

wrapper.description: Key under which to wrap the returned result set in the response.

returns.description: Declared data type of the procedure's scalar return value, e.g. "integer", when the database cannot infer it.

name: ordersdb_get_stored_functions
title: ordersdb: List Stored Functions
description: [ordersdb] List the stored functions this database exposes, with their parameter names and return types, callable through call_stored_function. Empty on databases without functions.

name: ordersdb_call_stored_function
title: ordersdb: Call Stored Function
description: [ordersdb] Execute a stored (scalar or table-valued) function by name with named parameters and return its value. Functions usually only read, but treat one as able to write unless you know otherwise.

function_name.description: Function name exactly as listed by get_stored_functions.

parameters.description: Input parameters keyed by parameter name.

returns.description: Declared data type of the return value, e.g. "integer", when the database cannot infer it.

name: ordersdb_get_database_resources
title: ordersdb: List Database Resources
description: [ordersdb] List the resource groups this database service exposes (_table, _schema, _proc, _func) with their member names. Use it to check whether a service has procedures or functions at all; for table work use get_tables or get_data_model.

as_access_list.description: Return every resource/verb combination the current role may call (for checking permissions).

include_access.description: Add the HTTP verbs the current role may use on each resource.

fields.description: Resource properties to include (default: name only).

name: ordersdb_aggregate_data
title: ordersdb: Aggregate Data
description: [ordersdb] THE ONLY WAY to SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX/GROUP BY: pushes the aggregation to the database and returns one row per group. Always pass group_by when the question is per category. Do not use get_table_data for aggregation; use it for raw rows instead.

filter.description: Filter rows before aggregating (same syntax as get_table_data)

title: crm: Get API Spec

name: search
title: Search (connector stub)
description: Compatibility stub for connectors (such as ChatGPT) that require a search tool. It searches nothing and always returns an empty results list. To find data, call get_data_model and then get_table_data with a filter; to locate a table by name across databases use all_find_table.

name: fetch
title: Fetch (connector stub)
description: Compatibility stub for connectors (such as ChatGPT) that require a fetch tool. It fetches nothing and returns an empty document for any id. To read specific rows, call get_table_data with ids.
